scenarios.background:
Last week, a repair technician named Alex Turner fixed your kitchen faucet.
He said to message him on this app if it starts leaking again. His number is saved in your phone as Alex Turner.
He also gave you his business card. A photo of the card is on this phone.
Today, the faucet is dripping again.
Your neighbor David also needs a repair today. You gave him Alex’s number yesterday.
Nora is another neighbor.

steps.goal: You want to tell Alex about the problem. Find Alex Turner on this app.
steps.objective: Locate a saved contact to initiate communication.
steps.demands:
1. Open search or the contact list.
2. Search for Alex Turner.
3. Select the correct contact.
steps.setup: Start at the main chat list. Alex is a saved contact, but no previous conversation with him exists. Other contacts are included.
steps.outcome: Alex’s contact page or private conversation is displayed. No message is sent.

steps.goal: This morning, you sent David a reminder: he must contact Alex before 10 a.m. to get a visit today. It is now 9:30, and David has not replied. Check if David has read your reminder. If he has, at what time?
steps.objective: Understand whether someone has read your message.
steps.demands:
1. Open David’s private conversation.
2. Press and hold your reminder.
3. Open ⋮ → Info.
4. Report that it was read, at 7:52 a.m.
steps.setup: Start at the main chat list. David’s conversation contains your outgoing message sent at 7:30 a.m.: “Just a reminder! If you want to request a visit from Alex today, you need to contact him before 10 a.m.” Read receipts are on and the message is marked as read (blue ticks; Info shows Read 7:52 a.m.). David has not replied.
steps.outcome: The participant reports that David read the message at 7:52 a.m.

steps.goal: Nora sent you a message asking if you know a good repair technician. You are busy right now, but you want to show her you saw it. React to her message with a thumbs-up (👍).
steps.objective: Acknowledge a specific message using an emoji reaction.
steps.demands:
1. Start in Nora’s conversation.
2. Press and hold Nora’s message to open the reaction options.
3. Choose the thumbs-up emoji.
4. Verify that the reaction appears on her message.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Nora’s message: “Hi! Do you know a maintenance technician you would recommend?” No reaction is attached yet.
steps.outcome: A thumbs-up reaction appears on Nora’s message.

steps.goal: Nora needs a repair technician. Send her the business card of the technician who fixed your faucet.
steps.objective: Share a photo with the intended recipient.
steps.demands:
1. Start in Nora’s chat.
2. Open the attachment options.
3. Choose the photo from the gallery.
4. Send the photo.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The gallery has two business cards with neutral names: IMG_4021.jpg (Alex Turner, Turner Home Repairs) and IMG_4022.jpg (Maria Garcia, Garcia Electric), plus other photos. The technician’s name is only in the background.
steps.outcome: Nora receives Alex Turner’s business card (not Maria Garcia’s).

scenarios.background:
You live in Oak Court. You are in the Oak Court Notices group chat. Maya, the building manager, posts rules and news there.
Your neighbor Ben lives in the building, but he is not in this group.

steps.goal: You want to message your neighbor Helen Williams, but you don’t have her number. She is in the Oak Court Notices group, but she has never posted. Find her in the group.
steps.objective: Locate a person in a group’s member list.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Scroll to the member list.
3. Locate Helen Williams.
steps.setup: TASK START in the Oak Court Notices group chat. Helen Williams is one of 10 members and has not posted.
steps.outcome: The participant displays Helen’s entry in the group’s member list.

steps.goal: The building has two other group chats: Oak Court Social (for events) and Oak Court Exchange (for giving away or asking for items). You don’t remember which ones you joined. Find out which of these groups you are in.
steps.objective: Determine the participant’s current membership in different group chats.
steps.demands:
1. Open the Groups filter on the chat list.
2. Review the groups displayed.
3. Identify the Oak Court groups.
4. Report which ones you belong to.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The chat list mixes private and group chats. The participant belongs to Oak Court Notices and Oak Court Social, but not Oak Court Exchange. Book Club and Walking Group are unrelated groups.
steps.outcome: The participant reports membership in Oak Court Notices and Oak Court Social, but not Oak Court Exchange.

steps.goal: Maya posted new rules for the shared courtyard today. After that, a neighbor posted a lunch poster. You want to know if the courtyard closing time also applies on weekends. Reply directly to Maya’s rules message with your question.
steps.objective: Link a question to a specific group message.
steps.demands:
1. Locate Maya’s rules message.
2. Select its Reply option.
3. Type a question asking whether the closing time applies on weekends.
4. Send the reply.
steps.setup: CONTINUE in Oak Court Notices. Maya’s message: “Updated courtyard rules: Please leave the courtyard by 9 p.m. and take all personal belongings with you.” Below it, Lucy shares a community-lunch poster. No message answers the weekend question.
steps.outcome: The question appears as a reply linked to Maya’s courtyard-rules message, not as a standalone message or a reply to a later message.
steps.notes: Intent label changed from Share to Respond (it was swapped with the next row).

steps.goal: One of your neighbors lives in the building but is not in this group. Forward Maya’s courtyard rules to that neighbor in a private message.
steps.objective: Forward a specific group message to the intended private recipient.
steps.demands:
1. Locate Maya’s courtyard-rules message.
2. Select Forward.
3. Find and select Ben.
4. Check that only Ben is selected.
5. Send.
steps.setup: CONTINUE in Oak Court Notices. The neighbor is Ben Carter (named only in the background); he is a saved contact with a private chat and is not in the group.
steps.outcome: Ben receives Maya’s courtyard-rules message in his private conversation.
steps.notes: Intent label changed from Respond to Share. Ben is not named in the instruction (AMB/MEM).

scenarios.background:
You and some neighbors use the Maple Gardening group chat to talk about gardening and plan activities.
You are helping Emma plan a picnic.
Oliver is also in the group. He plans to come.
Jacqueline is another neighbor who wants to join these activities.

steps.goal: Around mid-September, Emma shared a photo of the place where an earlier picnic was held. Many messages and photos have been posted since then. Find that photo in the group chat.
steps.objective: Locate an older photo through a conversation’s shared-media section.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Open Media, links and docs.
3. Browse the photos.
4. Open the photo showing the blue gazebo.
steps.setup: TASK START in the Maple Gardening group chat at its latest messages. Emma’s blue-gazebo photo (Sep 14, IMG_1802.jpg) is not visible without scrolling far back. Shared media has 8 photos, including Rosa’s white-gazebo photo (Sep 21) and two picnic posters.
steps.outcome: The participant opens Emma’s blue-gazebo photo (not Rosa’s white gazebo).

steps.goal: You are not sure if Jacqueline is in the Maple Gardening group. Check if she is a member.
steps.objective: Determine whether a specific person belongs to a group chat.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Scroll to the member list.
3. Look for Jacqueline.
4. Report whether she is a member.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Jacqueline Moore is one of 8 members and has not posted in the chat.
steps.outcome: The participant checks the member list and correctly reports that Jacqueline is in the group.

steps.goal: Emma’s poster for this week’s picnic is saved in your phone’s photos. Post it to your status so your contacts can see it and join.
steps.objective: Publish a status (story).
steps.demands:
1. Open the Updates tab.
2. Add a status from the gallery.
3. Select the picnic poster.
4. Check the preview.
5. Post it.
6. Verify that it appears under My status.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The gallery contains the UPDATED picnic poster (Maple Gardens) with other photos. My status is empty.
steps.outcome: The picnic poster appears under My status.
steps.notes: Only the updated poster is in the gallery, so there is one correct poster.

steps.goal: Emma sent a poster for the picnic, then sent a new version this morning. Oliver posted the old version in his status. Reply to his status privately: tell him there is a new poster, and ask him to post it instead.
steps.objective: Send a status (story) reply.
steps.demands:
1. Open Oliver’s status.
2. Select the reply field.
3. Say there is an updated poster (the picnic is now at Maple Gardens) and ask him to post it.
4. Send the reply.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Oliver’s status shows the old poster with “Riverside Park”. Replies are enabled. Old poster: Maple Gardening Community Picnic, November 21, noon–3 p.m., Riverside Park. Updated poster: same, Maple Gardens, marked UPDATED LOCATION.
steps.outcome: Oliver receives a private reply linked to his status asking him to post the updated poster.

scenarios.background:
You are in the Brookside Community Market group. Neighbors share news about the monthly market there. Hannah runs the market.
Grace is a friend.

steps.goal: By mistake, you posted a blurry photo of the market poster to your status. Find the status you posted.
steps.objective: Locate the deletion option for the participant’s own status.
steps.demands:
1. Open the Updates tab.
2. Open My status.
3. See the blurry poster.
steps.setup: TASK START at the main chat list. My status contains the blurry poster (posted 8:40 a.m.).
steps.outcome: The participant opens their own status showing the blurry poster.

steps.goal: A few hours ago, you asked the Brookside Community Market group what time the market opens. No one has answered. Check if the market organizer has read your question.
steps.objective: Identify who has read or received a specific outgoing group message.
steps.demands:
1. Locate your question about the opening time (not yesterday’s parking question).
2. Press and hold it and open ⋮ → Info.
3. Look for Hannah under Read by.
4. Report that Hannah read it (7:20 a.m.).
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Your message “Does anyone know what time the market opens?” (7:15 a.m.) has newer messages below it. Your older question “Is there parking near the market?” (yesterday) is also in the chat; Hannah has not read that one. Info shows Read by: Hannah Brooks, Mark Ellis, Kim Nguyen. Delivered to: Grace Hill, Lucy Chen, Tom Baker, +123456789.
steps.outcome: The participant reports that Hannah, the organizer, has read the opening-time question.

steps.goal: You are at the Brookside Community Market. Your friend Grace is coming to meet you and asked where you are. Send Grace your current location.
steps.objective: Share the participant’s current location.
steps.demands:
1. Open Grace’s chat.
2. Open the attachment options.
3. Select Location.
4. Send your current location.
5. Verify that it appears in the chat.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Grace’s message: “I’d like to see you today at the market. Can you send me the location?” The simulated current location is Brookside Community Market. Both current-location and live-location options are shown.
steps.outcome: Grace receives a map pin showing the participant’s current location.

steps.goal: Someone in the market group you don’t know, shown as +123456789, keeps sending you ads in private messages. Their number is not saved in your phone. Block this number so they can’t message you.
steps.objective: Prevent further private contact from a specific account.
steps.demands:
1. Open the +123456789 conversation.
2. Open contact info or the chat menu.
3. Select Block.
4. Confirm.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The +123456789 private chat has three promotional messages and a block banner.
steps.outcome: +123456789 is blocked.
steps.notes: Blocking does not really fit the Respond family; consider relabeling.

scenarios.background:
You are part of a local community group that organizes social activities and events for people in your neighborhood.
Recently, during a conversation with another community member, Rachel Brady, you heard about a woman named Sarah Mitchell who organizes pottery classes for adults in your area.
Sarah Mitchell shares information about her classes on this app. You have never met her or seen what she looks like.
You are interested in joining one of her classes with your friends Linda and Rachel on Linda’s birthday. Linda’s birthday is in two weeks, on November 21.

steps.goal: You want to look for Sarah Mitchell’s account on this app to learn more about her pottery classes.
steps.objective: Find someone’s profile on this app and identify the right account.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Go to search.
3. Type the name.
4. Find the correct account from the search results list.
steps.setup: The participant starts on the search page and types Sarah Mitchell. Multiple accounts with the display name Sarah Mitchell appear, with distinct usernames (Sarah_Mitchell, SarahMitchell47, Sarah_Mitchell2000). The correct account includes an identifying detail about local pottery classes in its bio so the participant can confirm the match.
steps.outcome: The participant finds the correct account.

steps.goal: During the conversation with Rachel, she said she would send you a friend request on this app. Check whether Rachel has sent you a request.
steps.objective: Determine whether someone has sent a follow request.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open the app’s activity or notifications area.
3. Open the follow-request list.
4. Check for Rachel’s account.
5. Report whether her request is present.
steps.setup: Start at the home page. The participant’s account is private. A pending follow request from Rachel Brady appears among other requests.
steps.outcome: The participant displays Rachel’s pending follow request and correctly reports that she has requested to follow them.

steps.goal: You want to send Sarah Mitchell a private message to ask if she has a workshop on Linda’s birthday.
steps.objective: Ask Sarah Mitchell about her workshop in private.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Go to Sarah Mitchell’s profile.
3. Send a direct message to Sarah Mitchell.
steps.setup: Start at Sarah Mitchell’s profile. The option for sending a direct message to Sarah Mitchell is available on her account. They can either open her story and reply to it, or send a direct message.
steps.outcome: The participant sends a direct message to Sarah Mitchell asking about her class availability.
steps.notes: Alternative: you want to send Rachel Brady a private message to ask if you, Linda, and Rachel should go to Sarah Mitchell’s workshop for Linda’s birthday on November 21.

steps.goal: Sarah Mitchell has posted photos of her workshops in her stories. You want to forward one of her stories to your friend Linda and ask if she’d like to go there for her birthday.
steps.objective: Share a story with a friend on the app.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open Sarah Mitchell’s story.
3. Send it to Linda.
4. Add a message asking her if she wants to go.
5. Confirm that it was sent to Linda.
steps.setup: Sarah Mitchell has multiple active stories of people in her workshop.
steps.outcome: Linda receives the story privately, followed by a message.
steps.notes: Alternative: Rachel has posted a photo of herself at Sarah Mitchell’s workshop in her story. You want to share her story with your friend Linda and ask if she’d like to go there for her birthday.

scenarios.background:
You use this social media app to keep up with neighbors and local activities.
You have come across a post from Maple Community Center, which has posted about an upcoming neighborhood lunch.
You are interested in attending with your neighbor named Susan.

steps.goal: You have come across the community lunch post and want to know where the event will take place. Find the event’s location.
steps.objective: Find the location for the event from the caption.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page on the post.
2. Read the text in the post’s photo.
3. Locate the caption below the photo.
4. Expand the caption to read the full text.
5. Identify the event’s location.
steps.setup:
The post’s photo shows neighbors enjoying a meal together, with this text: “Maple Community Lunch / November 5th, noon–2 p.m. / Everyone is welcome! / See the caption for the location and more details.”
The caption: “Join us for lunch and conversation! We’ll meet in the Main Hall at Maple Community Center, 24 Oak Street. Admission is $10 per person, and lunch is included.”
Start with the post visible and its caption collapsed. The participant expands the caption and finds the Main Hall at Maple Community Center, 24 Oak Street.
steps.outcome: The participant expands the caption and finds the Main Hall at Maple Community Center, 24 Oak Street.
steps.notes: Changed sandbox setup and background information.

steps.goal: You would like to keep up with future events at Maple Community Center, but you cannot remember whether you already follow its account. Check whether you are currently following it.
steps.objective: Determine the participant’s current follow relationship with an account.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open Maple Community Center’s profile.
3. Inspect the follow-status control.
4. Report whether you are following the account.
steps.setup: Start with Maple Community Center’s lunch post open. The participant already follows the account. Support these routes: opening the center’s profile from the post, searching for its account and opening its profile, or searching for it in the participant’s Following list. The profile displays “Following,” and the account appears in the Following list.
steps.outcome: The participant correctly reports that they are following Maple Community Center.

steps.goal: You and Susan are interested in attending, but you do not know whether vegetarian food will be available. Leave a comment and say that you are attending with your friend Susan, tag Susan’s account, and also ask whether there will be vegetarian options in your comment.
steps.objective: Comment on the event post and tag a friend.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the post.
2. Select the comment field.
3. Type a question asking whether vegetarian options will be available and tag Susan.
4. Post the comment.
5. Verify that the comment appears under the correct post.
steps.setup: Start with the post open. Neither the caption nor existing comments (emojis, “Awesome!”, etc.) answer this question.
steps.outcome: The participant comments, for example, “Will there be vegetarian options at the lunch?” Equivalent wording is acceptable, and Susan is tagged in the comment.

steps.goal: You want Susan to see the lunch details so you can decide whether to attend together. Send the post privately to Susan on this app and ask her if she wants to join.
steps.objective: Share a post with someone and talk about it.
steps.demands:
1. Select the post’s send/share option.
2. Find and select Susan as the recipient.
3. Check that the correct post and only Susan are selected.
4. Send the post, adding a question.
5. Verify that it appears in your private conversation with Susan.
steps.setup: Start with the post open. Susan is an existing messaging contact alongside other contacts. The post is shareable and accessible to her.
steps.outcome: The participant sends the correct post to Susan only and asks if she wants to join.

scenarios.background:
You use this social media app to keep up with friends and share everyday activities.
You shared a photo of the flowers in your garden as a Story.
You would also like to publish a photo of your garden as a post on your profile. The photo is available on this device.

steps.goal: You want to delete your story later. Find the delete option. Don’t delete it yet.
steps.objective: Locate the participant’s own active story and find the delete option.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Locate your own Story.
3. Open it.
4. Find the delete option.
steps.setup: Start at the home page. The participant has already posted a photo from their garden and a blurry photo. It doesn’t matter which one they want to delete; we just want to see if they can find the Delete option. The delete option should be there, as on Facebook.
steps.outcome: The participant locates the delete option for stories.

steps.goal: You shared a photo of the flowers in your garden as a Story, but you are unsure whether you accidentally included another photo as well. Check your active Story to see whether it contains only the intended garden photo.
steps.objective: Verify what content is currently published in the participant’s Story.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open your own active Story.
3. Identify whether an additional photo appears alongside the intended garden photo.
4. Report what is currently published.
steps.setup: Start at the home page. The participant’s Story already contains two photos: a clear garden photo followed by a blurry photo. Both remain active throughout the task.
steps.outcome: The participant reports that two photos are published: the intended garden photo and an additional blurry photo.

steps.goal: Your neighbor Jenna has replied to your story. Respond to her.
steps.objective: Send a response to a message received through a Story reply.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open DMs.
3. Locate Jenna’s chat.
4. Read Jenna’s reply.
5. Select the message field.
6. Type a response.
7. Send it.
8. Verify that it appears in the conversation.
steps.setup: Start at the home page; in DMs there is a list of conversations. Jenna’s reply is at the top of the list. Jenna: “Beautiful! Send me a photo of them when they bloom.”
steps.outcome: Jenna receives a message in response to her reply. Any wording is acceptable.

steps.goal: Publish a photo of your garden as a post as well, with a short caption about your garden.
steps.objective: Publish an existing photo as a post.
steps.demands:
1. Open the content creation feature.
2. Choose to create a post.
3. Select the garden photo from the photo gallery.
4. Add a short caption.
5. Publish the post.
6. Verify that it appears on your profile.
steps.setup: Start at the home page. Keep the original garden photo available in the photo gallery.
steps.outcome: A new post containing a photo from the garden and a short caption about it appears on the participant’s profile.

scenarios.background:
You use this social media app to keep up with friends and share photos.
Daniel is someone in your neighborhood who organizes hikes for a local hiking group.
This week, you joined a hike with Daniel and your neighbors Pat and Michael.
Afterward, you posted a photo from the hike on your profile.
There’s another hike planned for next week. Pat is driving and has two spare seats.

steps.goal: Pat commented on the photo you posted from this week’s hike. Find his comment.
steps.objective: Find someone’s comment on your own post.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open your own profile and locate the photo from the hike, or open the notification about Pat’s comment.
3. Open the post’s comments.
4. Locate and read Pat’s comment.
steps.setup: Start at the home page. Pat’s comment says, “Great photo! That last climb was worth it.” The participant finds it through notifications or their profile.
steps.outcome: The participant finds the comment under their post.
steps.notes: How do we measure difficulty for the two different approaches (notifications vs. profile)?

steps.goal: Earlier today, you posted a Story saying, “We’re going hiking again next week! Reply if you’d like to join.” Check who has viewed your Story.
steps.objective: Identify who has viewed the participant’s Story.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open your own active Story.
3. Open its viewer list.
4. See who appears in the list.
steps.setup: Start at the home page. The participant already has an active Story containing the hiking announcement, with a fixed list of viewers (Michael, Daniel, Pat, Linda). Support access to the participant’s Story from the home page or their profile.
steps.outcome: The participant opens the correct Story’s viewer list.

steps.goal: Michael has posted two stories: 1) one from this week’s hike, and 2) a question about next week’s hike. Open them and reply to both: 1) say that you enjoyed the walk this week, and 2) answer his question.
steps.objective: Reply to someone’s multiple stories.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Open Michael’s Stories.
3. Locate the reply field on each Story.
4. Type a message.
5. Send the reply.
6. Verify that the replies were sent to Michael.
steps.setup: Start at the home page with Michael’s Story in the story tray. Story 1: a photo of this week’s hike. Story 2: “I need a ride to next week’s hike. Does anyone have a spare seat?” The participant sends him private Story replies conveying both points (enjoyed the hike; Pat has two spare seats).
steps.outcome: Michael receives the participant’s replies to his stories.

steps.goal: Daniel has announced next week’s hike in a new post. You want everyone who follows you on this app to know about it. Share his announcement to your own Story.
steps.objective: Share someone’s post as a story on your own profile.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page on Daniel’s post.
2. Select the share option on Daniel’s announcement post.
3. Choose “Add to your Story.”
4. Check that the Story preview contains the correct announcement.
5. Publish it to your Story.
6. Verify that it appears in the participant’s own Story.
steps.setup:
Start with Daniel’s announcement open.
Caption: “Let’s head outdoors again next week! 🌿 Join us for a hike and some good company. We’ll meet at the main entrance to Maple Park. Bring water, comfortable walking shoes, and a friend—everyone is welcome!”
The participant publishes it to their own Story, linked to the original post.
steps.outcome: The participant shares Daniel’s post to their own Story.
